2026-12-22.title: 22 December · Advent Weekday (O King of Nations)
readings: Hannah gives thanks for the birth of Samuel
My heart exults in the Lord, my Saviour
The Mighty One has done great things for me
2026-12-22.alt: O Antiphon: O Rex Gentium (O King of Nations).
2026-12-22.verse: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O King of the nations and their desire, the cornerstone who makes both one: come and save the human race, which you fashioned from clay.” Hannah, once barren and mocked, brings the child Samuel to the house of the Lord at Shiloh and gives him back to God: “For this child I prayed… Therefore I have lent him to the LORD.” Her song (today's responsorial psalm) sings of a God who “raises up the poor from the dust”.

Mary's Magnificat echoes Hannah's song almost line by line. The humble servant of Nazareth magnifies the Lord who “has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant”. Then she sings of a great reversal: the proud scattered, the powerful brought down, the lowly lifted up, the hungry filled, the rich sent away empty. This is not a political programme but the logic of the Kingdom: God's power is shown in mercy to the humble. The Church sings the Magnificat every evening at Vespers.
outline: Ask: what has God done for you this year? Name one great thing.
What God gives, Hannah gives back.
God lifts the lowly and fills the hungry.
He remembers his mercy to Abraham.
“The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
live: Pray Mary's song slowly each evening until Christmas.
Help a poor family prepare for Christmas.
2026-12-22.prayer: O King of the nations, cornerstone who makes all one, come and save us whom you formed from clay. With Mary and Hannah, let my soul magnify you, and make me generous to the lowly and the hungry. Amen.
altar: At Mass we offer back to God the bread and wine he has given us, and he returns them as the Body and Blood of his Son.

quick: Hannah gave back to God the son he gave her.
Mary sings the great reversal of God's Kingdom.
2026-12-22.action: Pray the Magnificat each evening until Christmas.
2026-12-22.question: What great thing has God done for me this year?

family.explain: Mary sang a song of praise because God loves the humble and feeds the hungry.
family.intention: We pray for vocations from our families, and for the hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift from God can we give back by sharing it?”

pm.open: O King of the nations, cornerstone who makes both one, come and save the human race. Lord, with Mary and Hannah we gather to magnify you. Amen.
share: Hannah said: I have lent him to the Lord (1 Samuel 1:28). What gift do I need to give back to God?
Mary says God lifts up the lowly (Luke 1:52). Do I trust God's way of choosing the small?
What words of the Magnificat speak to me today?
interc: For the Church, that she may always sing the praises of God.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life.
For the hungry and the lowly, that God may lift them up.
For the powerful, that they may use their power with justice.
For our families, that we may be grateful and generous.
pm.close: Lord God, you looked on the lowliness of Mary and heard the prayer of Hannah. Give us humble and grateful hearts, and accept the gifts we offer back to you. Amen.

illus: A mother in Kannur, when her son told her he wanted to be a priest, cried at first. Then she remembered Hannah. At his ordination she said: “God gave him to me. Today I give him back.”

homily: Dear friends, today's O Antiphon prays: O King of the nations, and their desire, the cornerstone who makes both one: come and save the human race, which you fashioned from clay.

In the first reading Hannah brings the young Samuel to the house of the Lord at Shiloh. She had prayed for a child; now she gives him back: for this child I prayed, and the Lord has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the Lord (1 Samuel 1:27–28). Then Hannah sings: my heart exults in the Lord (1 Samuel 2:1).

In the Gospel Mary sings her Magnificat: my soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Saviour, for he has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant (Luke 1:46–48). Hannah's song and Mary's song are sisters: both praise the God who lifts up the lowly.

Mary sings that God has brought down the powerful from their thrones and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty (Luke 1:52–53). This is God's way: he chooses the small.
Hannah gave back the gift she had received. Mary gave her whole self. Both teach us that what God gives us is not ours to keep, but to offer back to him: our children, our talents, our lives.

Let us pray the Magnificat slowly today, perhaps as a family. Let us give back to God one gift he has given us, by using it for others. And let us ask Mary to give us humble, grateful hearts as we approach Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sang a song of joy because God loves the poor and the humble. Sing a song to God today!

intro: Hannah's gift, Mary's song, and the great reversal of God's Kingdom.

sub: She gave the child back to God.
q: For this child I prayed; and the LORD has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD.
For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name. His mercy is for those who fear him from generation to generation.
points.apply: Offer back to God one gift he has given you.

q: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honor.

He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts. He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.
points.apply: Help a poor family prepare for Christmas.

sub: God promised Abraham a blessing for all.
q: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
He has helped his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy, according to the promise he made to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his descendants forever.
points.apply: Thank God for a promise kept in your family.

concl: God's power is shown in mercy to the humble.
Let our souls magnify the Lord.
